rules.name: Temporal and Geographic Electives
rules.desc:
Majors must take two courses in each of 6 Distribution Categories: three temporal and three geographic.
Any individual course satisfies one temporal and one geographic category. Courses listed in multiple temporal or geographic categories may count toward only one temporal and one geographic requirement (a single course may not be used to satisfy multiple temporal or geographic requirements). Survey Courses and courses taken in the Area of Concentration may apply toward Distribution Categories.
Completing a full year of ITALIC or SLE may count as an Art History elective.

rules.name: Temporal Distribution Categories
rules.desc: A given course may only be used once to satisfy the below temporal distribution categories.

rules.name: Geographic Distribution Categories
rules.desc: A given course may only be used once to satisfy the below geographic distribution categories.

rules.name: Film & Media Studies Course
rules.desc:
Complete any four- or five-unit Film & Media Studies (FILMEDIA) course.
Survey courses, FILMEDIA 4 Introduction to Film Study and FILMEDIA 6 Media and Mediums, and the FILMEDIA courses within the 1850 to Present Temporal Distribution may count towards this requirement.

rules.name: Remaining units of the 65-unit minimum, in Art History
Area of Concentration
rules.desc:
The department encourages students to pursue their interests by designing an area of concentration tailored to their intellectual concerns. This area of concentration provides the student with an in-depth understanding of a coherent topic in Art History.
The student’s faculty advisor approves concentrations within the major; they are not declared on Axess and do not appear on the transcript or the diploma. Sample concentrations can be found on the department website.
By Winter Quarter of their junior year, students must complete an area of concentration form, identifying their chosen concentration and three courses to fulfill it.

• Seminar course: one seminar (200-level) course within the area of concentration

• Two additional courses: two ARTHIST courses of any level within the area of concentration

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.desc: This course is designed for Art History majors in their junior year, equipping them with the scholarly tools necessary for writing about art in various contexts as they progress through the major.

rules.name: Capstone Junior Seminar
rules.desc: This course is designed to introduce majors to methods and theories underlying the practice of Art History. The seminar is offered annually, typically during Autumn Quarter.

rules.name: Honors

children.name: 10 units of ARTHIST 297 in the senior year
Honors thesis submitted to the advisor and second reader
GPA of 3.5 overall and in Art History courses

rules.desc:
The purpose of the honors program is to extend and deepen work done in Art History classes. The honors thesis topic typically emerges from prior coursework; it should be focused and have clear parameters. Ordinarily, an honors thesis is an exploration of an area the student has already studied.
Admission to the Honor Program
The minimum requirement for admission to the honors program is an overall GPA of 3.5 and at least 3.5 in Art History courses. Students must complete at least five Art History courses at Stanford by the end of their junior year, and four must be completed by the end of Winter Quarter.
Submission of the Thesis Proposal
Candidates for the honors program must submit a five-page (double-spaced) thesis proposal, including bibliography and illustrations, and one completed paper that demonstrates the student’s ability to conceptualize and write cogently about art historical issues. A complete application is due to the proposed thesis advisor on March 31.
Submission and Approval of the Honors Thesis
Students must submit the final draft of their honors thesis to their faculty advisor, the second faculty reader, the Student Services Specialist, and the Honors Director by the thesis deadline.
More Information
For more information about the Art History and Film & Media Studies Honors Program, students can visit the department website.
rules.notes: Honors students must complete a total of 10 units of ARTHIST 297 during their senior year.

grading: Courses must be taken for at least four units and for a letter grade.
policies: Eligible students may also pursue a Bachelor of Arts in Art History with Honors.
transferPolicy: Students can take a maximum of two courses (10 units) away from Stanford; this includes transfer courses from other universities and Stanford Bing Overseas Studies Program. Students must meet with their faculty advisor and the Student Services Specialist before planning an overseas campus program.
reviewNotes: Every course must be taken for a letter grade and for at least four units, toward the 65 units the major needs; ARTHIST courses beyond the named requirements count toward that total. The audit checks the core courses, a 4-unit ARTSTUDI course, three survey courses, two courses in each temporal category and each geographic category, and a FILMEDIA course. A course fills one temporal and one geographic category, and survey, concentration and FILMEDIA courses may also fill categories; the audit cannot stop one course from filling two geographic categories, so check that yourself. You check by hand the three-course area of concentration, the library orientation, at most two courses (10 units) taken away from Stanford, and for honors 10 units of ARTHIST 297, the thesis and the 3.5 GPAs.
